slides.heading: What Is Punctuation?
bullets: Punctuation is the art of dividing writing into sentences and parts by points and marks.
The marks show the reader where to pause and how the parts fit together.
The chief marks:  period ( . )  question mark ( ? )  exclamation point ( ! )
…and  comma ( , )  semicolon ( ; )  colon ( : )  dash ( — )  parentheses ( ).

slides.heading: End Marks
bullets: A Period ( . ) ends a statement or a command:  “The sky is blue.”  “Shut the door.”
A Question Mark ( ? ) ends a question:  “Where are you going?”
An Exclamation Point ( ! ) shows strong feeling:  “Watch out!”
Every sentence ends with one of these three marks.

slides.heading: Practice — Which End Mark?
slides.instruction: Choose the right end mark:  .  ?  or  !

slides.heading: The Comma
bullets: A comma shows the slightest pause between parts of a sentence.
Use it in a series of three or more:  “red, white, and blue.”
Use it after a greeting or opening word:  “Yes, I will come.”  “Hi, Mom.”
Use it to join two sentences with and, but, or:  “We ran, and we won.”

slides.heading: Practice — Add the Commas
slides.instruction: Write each phrase with its commas added.

slides.heading: More Marks
bullets: Semicolon ( ; ) — a bigger pause than a comma, joining two related sentences.
Colon ( : ) — introduces a list or a quotation:  “Bring these: milk, eggs, bread.”
Apostrophe ( ’ ) — shows ownership or a contraction:  “John’s,” “don’t.”
Quotation Marks ( “ ” ) — frame someone’s exact words.

slides.heading: Practice — Name the Mark
slides.instruction: Name the punctuation mark that does each job.

slides.heading: The Dash & Parentheses
bullets: A Dash ( — ) marks a sudden break or a change of thought:  “I was sure — but no.”
Parentheses ( ) enclose an extra remark that could be left out.
“My gun was on my arm (as it always is) when I saw the rabbit.”
Use them sparingly — too many break up the reading.

items: When do we use commas in a series?
answers: The art of dividing writing with points and marks.
To separate three or more items.
